build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL/WebGPU renderer signal is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The core loop from the original brief is playable and completed through player input: Create a small 3D open world adventure demo, based on Three.js, using importmap to introduce ThreeJS, single HTML self-contained, no external models, textures, audio, all geometry and materials are generated programmatically. The program generates undulating grassy and mountainous terrain, and blocks the terrain blocks are stream-loaded; first-person character controller, WASD movement, mouse perspective, and jumping; distribution of NPCs, pick-up props, and interactive triggers; multiple branchable plots, triggered dialogue system; simple wild animal AI patrol; the goal is to find three ancient ruins to complete the main line; octree for collision detection; WebAudio synthesizes interactive sound effects. Art: low polygonal fantasy open world, day and night cycle, fog effects, dynamic skylight. Acceptance criteria: You can freely roam the large map, trigger multiple branch plots, and complete the main objectives. The plot branches will change the ending text; localStorage saves player progress. Output a single complete self-contained HTML file, use importmap to introduce threejs, zero external resources, and have a complete game closed loop: start interface, game loop, plot advancement, victory/settlement interface; localStorage stores progress; semi-finished demos are prohibited.
Core inputs, rules, state transitions, success conditions, and failure conditions form a deterministic state machine in game_logic.js rather than static buttons or decoration.
At least one core action exposes valid/invalid input, edge conditions, immediate feedback, and recovery or reset behavior.
Implement three escalating phases and make theme-appropriate resources, timers, health, score, inventory, cooldowns, or other state change decisions.
Provide at least three functionally distinct contents, objects, levels, enemies, puzzles, or strategic choices; color/text swaps alone do not count.
Implement pause, restart, result, localStorage restoration, and at least one observable persistent or replay outcome.
The third phase combines at least two earlier mechanics and provides clear success, failure, and replay flows.
The HUD clearly presents the objective, critical resources, phase, progress, and danger, synchronized with live state.
Valid, invalid, damage, success, failure, and state changes have distinguishable immediate feedback.
The complete start, onboarding, play, result, and retry loop works without a page refresh.
Use a coherent, recognizable original art direction in which the chosen technology serves the theme rather than default controls.
Camera, composition, layering, lighting, or 2D layout are deliberate and keep important objects and goals readable.
Actors, goals, hazards, tools, and UI symbols have readable silhouettes and visibly different functional states.
Movement, impacts, transitions, alerts, completion moments, and UI changes use multi-frame animation, particles, camera, or audio feedback.
